rationale.usefulness: A connector that preserves a familiar coding workflow while permitting model comparisons is useful to app and website builders. The report makes the trial actionable with fixed-model selection, billing boundaries, configuration details and task-level cost accounting; video usefulness is correctly limited to surrounding production tasks.
rationale.impact: This is an integration and provider-choice improvement, rather than a new model or training method. It could lower switching friction for existing users, but the supplied material does not demonstrate savings per completed task or broad changes to AI development. A four is independent of the current article length.
rationale.novelty: The combination of multiple agent/desktop surfaces, automatic routing and optional image workflows is a useful integration. Model routing and compatible-provider substitution are established ideas, and no comparative evidence here establishes a distinctly new capability.
rationale.maturity: The beta has detailed operational documentation, but its launch and current docs disagree about session-versus-request routing. Surface-specific behavior, mutable menus and the absence of any installed trial materially limit confidence in readiness.
rationale.openness: Hosted open-model choice can reduce dependence on a single model supplier, but access still runs through a hosted gateway and API accounts. The evidence does not establish connector licensing or rights for every model, and model openness cannot be attributed wholesale to the service.

concerns: Non-blocking: the routing contradiction remains unresolved; the report prominently discloses it and recommends a fixed-model trial rather than inventing a resolution.
Non-blocking: advertised savings and same-token Opus estimates do not establish equal-quality task savings.
Separate publication gate: this reviewer rates impact 4; if final mean impact is below 5, the contract requires the 1,000-word tier and fresh review after any substantive revision.
